7.2. Planning Business Capability Instance Increments

Many times, business capabilities cannot move to the final desired state in one step. There may also be dependencies that mean sequencing of capability increments needs to be coordinated. Depending on the gap that needs to be addressed, there could be sequencing where a business process change needs to occur ahead of an application enhancement. No matter the dependencies that would provide some form of stepwise change, one or more gaps being addressed together would be identified as a plateau; i.e., where the collection of enhancements to address the gaps preserve a functional value stream.

The architecture model will be able to identify the business capabilities that have gaps and where those gaps may have dependencies. The management of the resources and the timing of who will deliver the business capability enhancements through work packages is left to the project or program. A gap is indicated using the ArchiMate gap element, where the same gap assigned to multiple business capabilities shows a potential grouping.

Looking at the business capability improvements from the previous section, they would be modeled as follows:

• Optimize: The Delivery Management business capability instance will be enhanced by providing delivery drivers with a Signature Pad that sends the signature back to the shipping application; this gap at the business capability level seems small in the model but will take some time to design and implement

• Consolidate: The Modern Warehouse Management instance is upgraded to include Electronics Warehouse products

These have been modeled as gaps at the application level. Once the Modern Warehouse Management application has been enhanced, the Inventory Management instance using the Legacy Inventory Management application can be retired.

• Create: A new Incentive Management capability instance is going to be added to the first value stream, as shown in Figure 7-2

• Retire: This is illustrated in Figure 7-2, again at the application level

There are many business capabilities and associated value streams that depend on the Legacy Warehouse Management application. Since there is no real “gap” for the Legacy Warehouse Management application, mark that application with an event: “Retire Application”.

Figure 7-2: Addition of the Incentive Management Application

With the identified gaps a project manager or the operations teams can use the model to confirm timing based on team capacity and, where necessary, highlight dependencies that would affect the order in which these gaps would be addressed.

The gaps in the example are independent of each other except for retiring the Warehouse Management business capability that is instantiated using the Legacy Warehouse Management application. There will be situations where a series of gaps are identified that are all required to make the value stream execute effectively. This means that many teams will have to work together to coordinate their efforts using standard project management practices or more coordinated operational release management. [2]

section_title: 7.3. Digital Transformation and Business Capability Planning
text:
7.3. Digital Transformation and Business Capability

Planning

Digital Transformation is held at times to be a specialized form of innovation that is disproportionate to other forms of innovation. This perception is due to many factors including the pace of technology

section_title: 7.3. Digital Transformation and Business Capability Planning
text:
change, the inability of organizations to adapt at the same pace, and a fear of change that hinders the adoption of most innovation.

Business capability planning has the potential to make Digital Transformation less daunting and more achievable. While entire new value streams may be developed, they usually enhance or create new business capability instances that are combined with existing business capability instances that can be more rapidly implemented. When put in the light of value streams and business capabilities, new technologies can be seen better in the context of the stakeholders utilizing the organization’s value streams versus the innovative technology being the focal point with little to no context.

The use of technology – like any other resource leveraged to create or enhance a business capability instance – is really a component of an existing business capability instance. Using business capability planning models and techniques Enterprise and Business Architects can more effectively demonstrate how to best leverage these new technologies.

Endnotes

[1] Refer to: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic. [2] See Section B.2 and the notes on Agile Release Trains.

8. Conclusion

Business capability planning can be a powerful tool for Business and Enterprise Architects. Understanding value streams is a critical first step in being able to perform business capability planning. Creating and curating a business capability catalog provides a dictionary of terms to support dialog between different stakeholders.

Associating business capabilities to value streams and then modeling how those business capabilities have been instantiated provides the basis for further analysis. Value streams can be optimized by changing the business capability instances.

B: Other Frameworks

Business capability planning can form the basis to derive other models and fit with other frameworks. This appendix documents how business capability planning using value streams can inform these. Some sections highlight where there is usage of similar terms and describes the differences between them.

B.1. Business Process Modeling

Business process models have fewer formal boundaries or conditions than value streams and business capabilities. Business process models can be tightly or loosely aligned to value streams or the underlying business capabilities. Using business capability instances can provide the actors and many of the coarse-grained steps that can then be drilled down to a level deeper to provide more detailed dependencies and specifications.

A business or application process is one of the components of a business capability instance. While a system analyst may model at this level to build the specific business logic required in the application, business analysts rarely model a process at the business capability instance level.

What is more common is to create a business process at the value stream stage level. The actors and application interactions can be detailed in a sequence and swim-lane diagram by using Business Process Model and Notation™ (BPMN™) or a business process modeling language of choice. Here is where more detailed business process modeling will both be informed by and inform the value stream.

Some business processes will span value stream stages. Many business processes are written from only the human actor perspective; some are written for each actor in isolation to support training. Harmonizing the processes that are described in the business capability instances is not worth the effort. Having analysts working with architects to review their models is most certainly worth the effort.

text:
B.2. Scaled Agile Framework Enterprise Value Streams

The Scaled Agile Framework® enterprise (SAFe®) looks to help organizations who are interested in “… achieving business agility using Lean, Agile, and DevOps”.[1] If you are one of those organizations, business capability planning may be a valuable addition to create Operational value streams (see below) as well as defining an Agile Release Train.

[2]

SAFe Operational Value Streams

Within SAFe, the concept of value stream has many of the same aspects as described in this document. SAFe describes two classes of value stream: Operational and Development. The Operational value streams are in essence what has been described in this document. The Development value stream would describe the value stream and supporting business capability instances that allow for the development of enhancements or new IT assets that would improve individual business capability instances with an aim to streamline and optimize Operational value streams.

section_title: B.2. Scaled Agile Framework Enterprise Value Streams
text:
As noted on the SAFe website: “… most SAFe guidance focuses on helping the systems and software developers, product managers, engineers, scientists, IT practitioners, and others who work in Development value streams … However, the customers they serve live either in the company or at the end of the Operational value streams.”

Organizations who are using Agile or SAFe practices will be able to link between Operational and Development value streams using business capability planning at the business capability instance level.

Agile Release Trains [3] and Operational Value Streams

An Agile Release Train looks to align Agile product management teams’ backlog and enhancements by either the Operational or Development value streams they share or support. For a business capability planning Operational value stream, all the enhancements proposed for the Acquire Retail Product Online value stream would be added to the backlog for each of the affected product teams.

In the retail organization the CRM, Online Store, and the Modern Warehouse Management and Legacy Warehouse Management application teams are all different Agile teams. The enhancements proposed would result in two release trains that require coordination between two teams each.

The first release train would be the enhancement that bridges the Online Store Incentive Management integration with the CRM gap. The Agile teams can further break down the high-level business capability instance improvements recommended into the appropriate product enhancements and into the product backlog. From there, the proposed product release schedule can be determined and communicated to the appropriate stakeholders. The Agile Release Train will iterate until the enhancements required to support the business capability instances for this value stream are completed and the value those enhancements achieve can be measured.

The second release train would be when the Electronics Warehouse is able to move to use the Modern Warehouse Management application and the Legacy Warehouse Management application team can retire that application. This release train would be more complicated since both applications support many more Operational value streams than just the Acquire Retail Product Online value stream. This is again where business capability planning can help organizations that use SAFe to have inter- dependent roadmaps based on each portfolio.

B.3. Journey Maps

Value streams are usually triggered by stakeholders who derive value from them. A journey map is an analysis of the experience of a stakeholder through a series of touch points to understand how that experience can be improved. A journey map can be aligned to the value stream stages and the underlying business capability instances for analysis and improvement of the value stream.

Table B-1 shows a journey map based on the Acquire Retail Product Online value stream. The journey map extends the value stream by examining the customer experience for the stages that are under investigation. In this situation it is only for the online purchase and not the final value stream stage. The relevant touch points are added and assessed. The areas for improvement could then be mapped

B.4. Lean Value Stream

Lean value streams came out of the Lean Thinking movement, which originated in the automotive industry in Japan (at Toyota, the process is known as “material and information flow mapping”). The core premise of Lean Thinking is to identify and eliminate waste from a firm’s processes, with the goal of only retaining those activities that create or increase value for the end user. The lean value stream is a diagrammatic representation of the sequence of activities required to design, produce, and deliver a good or service to a customer (see Figure B-1). By adding performance metrics around each process (such as Processing Time, Response Time, and Percent Complete & Accurate), it becomes possible to use lean value streams to identify opportunities for waste reduction.

The lean value stream’s primary purpose is to document, analyze, and improve the flow of information or materials required to produce a product or service for a customer. This would seem to align to the business capability planning rationale as well. This invariably leads to the question: if the purposes are aligned, could the techniques also align?

There is a key abbreviation in the Lean Six Sigma[4] world called SIPOC (Suppliers, Inputs, Processes, Outputs, and Customers). Looking at a business capability planning value stream, it would cover the stakeholder, goals, and outcomes. Looking at the model above, processes and functions are combined to enable some form of analysis.

Using business capability planning techniques, lean concepts around waste through lead time and processing time could be used to see how efficiently each business capability instance is performing in support of a particular value stream stage or entire value stream.

B.5. Porter Value Chain

Value chains were introduced by Michael Porter in his book Competitive Advantage: Creating and Sustaining Superior Performance [Porter, 2004]; see Figure B-1.

“The value chain disaggregates a firm into its strategically-relevant activities in order to understand the behavior of costs and the existing potential sources of (competitive) differentiation.”

Figure B-1: Michael Porter’s Value Chain (Source: Competitive Advantage)

With its primary focus on activity costs and margins, the value chain perspective is concerned with understanding how economic value is created. Value chains provide a macro-level view of how a business produces economic value (i.e., money). Value chains, like the Business Model Canvas, usually model an entire organization or business unit. The value chain from that perspective can be informative as a basis to decide which value streams need to be modeled to ensure that the value chain operates.

B.6. Risk and Security Perspectives

Risk and security perspectives are pervasive throughout the organization. There may be some business capabilities specific to security such as Identity Management. There may also be processes that make a business capability instance, or goals or outcomes of the execution of a value stream. It also may be a value stream itself, such as when an investigation into theft within the retail organization has occurred.

The TOGAF® Series Guide: Integrating Risk and Security within a TOGAF Enterprise [G152] provides a guide to security controls and a linkage together with other standards.

C: Recruit Employee Value Stream

The Recruit Employee value stream was developed early in the process of writing this document. The authors decided to focus on a more customer-centric value stream for the examples. That said, with the work done, it would be useful to include this more back-office example.

As seen in the organization’s strategy, they are looking for revenue growth. That means that the ability to attract and hire new employees is key to the overall organization’s success. Currently, the value stream takes over twice as long to execute as the organization requires. Additionally, when the final candidate became an employee some skills gaps resulted. This value stream needs to reduce the current time to execute and improve the skills and experience alignment between the position that is posted and the eventual successful candidate.

The value stream has been broken down into the following five value stream stages that are also illustrated in Figure C-1. The value stream is initiated when a vacant position is created either as a new position or when an employee has left the organization:

• Define Position: The hiring manager reviews the required role for their team within the program for which they have responsibility

The HR advisor reviews the available role catalog and position descriptions to leverage one or more to adapt a position description. Finally, the finance analyst confirms that there is a sufficient compensation budget for the position.

• Communicate Open Position: Based on the position description, the recruiter creates the position in the recruiting application and then subsequently the company website and a contracted job posting website

Candidates respond through either channel by submitting a resumé and cover letter which is then migrated to a document repository. The HR advisor manually reviews each resumé to reject unqualified candidates to get to a “manageable” list of candidates.

• Select Final Candidates: The team of the hiring manager and the HR advisor review the shortlist of candidates to score the candidates to select a shortlist to interview

The shortlisted candidates are scheduled and interviewed. The scores are then adjusted to produce a ranked list of candidates to whom an offer will be extended.

• Offer Position: A review of the available salary bands provides the input required to create the employment contract that is sent to the candidate along with the pre-employment information documents

A final police check is required along with the signed contract to complete this value stream stage.

• Onboard Candidates: When the candidate presents for employment, they are provided with office space, credentials, as well as finalizing payroll and benefits information

At this point, the employee is not ready to be able to perform the role for which they have been hired.

An initial analysis of the value stream stages suggests the following business capabilities are required for each of the value stream stages. Also added are stage end points as well as the key stakeholders, trigger for the value stream, and goal for improving the value stream.

Magaly 目前正在其信息安全与基础设施（Information Security and Infrastructure）组织内实施业务架构和业务能力规划。她的志向是制定更以业务为重的投资策略，通过连接网络安全与技术来转变价值交付。

**Peter Ridgway——数字业务顾问，Fujitsu**

Peter 曾在英国和澳大利亚，以业务与 ICT 协调者的身份服务于政府、私营和学术部门。从业务与运营模型、风险与安全，到信息与技术，识别价值与目标、构建战略并交付成果是他的主要关注点。

## 1. 引言

许多组织在管理业务复杂性方面举步维艰。它们希望回答关于实现战略目标进度的问题：投资是否投向了正确的地方？是否存在适合整合的冗余或重复？企业是否具备成功所需的条件，或者是否拥有过多？

要回答这些问题，从业者需要先做功课：

- 理解组织的使命、愿景与价值观；
- 审视组织架构图、财务与可用业务计划；
- 在逻辑层面对 IT 进行编目。

这些资源是开展业务能力规划所必需的。

能力与价值流用于规划的概念已存在数十年。北约（NATO）曾用能力进行情景规划，试图抽象由成员国提供的军事单元；精益学科使用详细价值流图消除物料使用与信息流中的低效。The Open Group 已将能力、价值流与基于能力的规划概念纳入 TOGAF® 架构开发方法（ADM）、ArchiMate® 规范及众多指南。

价值流提供可视化手段，传达组织如何向客户与其他利益相关者交付价值。把价值流分解为具有退出标准与成果的逻辑阶段，可理解沿途为客户创造的关键价值方面；价值流阶段随后可映射到业务能力，以更好理解实现该价值流所需的条件。

业务能力目录对组织内许多受众都是极佳资源：它提供每项业务能力的定义，通常结合模型，使人能找到所需的业务能力。创建并维护业务能力目录工作量可观。

业务能力通过人员、流程与应用等工具实例化。把价值流建模到业务能力层，可洞察如何使价值流或阶段更高效、更有效。强烈建议从业者在这一分析层级使用共享的架构建模工具。

建模到业务能力实例层的价值流可被评估，以判断该实例是否有优化、整合、新建或退役的空间。当希望复用业务能力实例、使新价值流尽快投入运行时，可创建新的价值流。

业务能力规划利用抽象业务能力的力量汇聚多种视角。业务能力本身不是目的，而是组织价值流的构建块；持续优化现有价值流并创造新价值流的能力，是任何组织成功的关键。

本文档提供技术、推荐工具，并引用其他对业务能力规划有用的方法。

---

section_title: 2. 基于能力的规划的历史
text:
## 2. 基于能力的规划的历史

基于能力的规划由北约的研究与技术组织（RTO）研究、分析与仿真（SAS）小组提出。多国军事组织需要基于未来预期作战情景进行联合规划的能力。“（任务部队结构单元的）描述应能以能力术语表达其应执行的任务。一旦定义能力清单，就可推导出实现这些能力的最具成本效益与效率的实体部队单元选项。”[NATO]

军事规划者的建议是摆脱基于威胁的规划，探索若干潜在情景；把能力及能力“分段”映射到多个情景，评估能力满足各情景目标的程度；据此支持“哪些能力需要随时间投资”的判断——依据是哪些能力能应对最多情景。

Ulrich Homann 在微软工作期间撰写了《面向服务的业务导向基础》，其中把业务能力定义为：“……企业为达成特定目的或成果而可能拥有或交换的特定能力或才能……业务能力把人员、流程/程序、技术与信息抽象并封装为促进绩效改进与再设计分析所需的基本构建块。”[Homann, 2006]

在该面向服务框架中，抽象到业务能力使“能力连接器”得以暴露并提供“丰富的语义信息”。用能力对业务建模，为面向服务架构（SOA）提供业务语境。借助这一额外语境，人们希望使 IT 设计面向未来；它也被视为能够以更敏捷的方式满足业务需求。

1990 年，“价值流”一词出现在 James Womack 的《改变世界的机器》一书中 [Womack, 1991]。价值流评估为响应客户请求而执行的一系列活动或流程的效率。价值流图使精益从业者能够识别导致效率降低的浪费。价值流图基于丰田所使用的可视化技术，即“物料与信息流图”。

在过去的十年左右，能力与价值流已被加入 TOGAF ADM、各类指南以及 ArchiMate 建模语言，并新增了能力与价值流元素。

---

## 3. 业务能力规划建模

为有效执行业务能力规划，建议使用 ArchiMate 建模语言。ArchiMate 语言的明确目的是为描述整个企业的图提供统一视图；它对特定视图关键要素的精确定义及要素间允许的关系类型也很有用。

ArchiMate 语言与架构建模工具对从业者有用，但对一般或高管受众可能不够易读。本文档后文将提供带能力实例的详细价值流模型的抽象版本，展示从业者如何弥合不同受众之间的差距。

### 3.1 关键 ArchiMate 元素

ArchiMate 可跨所有架构域、层与方面建模。业务能力规划只需其中一部分元素即可支撑将要开发的模型。图 3-1 与表 3-1 给出本文档后续模型所用元素；其他元素也可能有用，但建议从该子集开始。

![图 3-1：ArchiMate 业务能力元素与关系](figs/g233_fig3-1.svg)

图 3-1 中的业务能力元素具有清晰的关系，有助于理解它们在能力与价值交付中的作用。这些元素与关系旨在用于价值流模型所表达的视角。表 3-1 说明这些元素与关系在业务能力规划语境中的用法。

**表 3-1：ArchiMate 业务能力元素与关系的用途**

| 元素 | 在业务能力规划中的用途 |
|---|---|
| 应用组件 | 封装与特定业务能力对齐的应用功能；也可封装其他应用组件。 |
| 应用过程 | 在业务能力实例语境中实现特定结果的应用行为序列。 |
| 业务能力 | 组织、人或系统等主动结构要素所拥有的能力。评估的关键在于：从业务能力目录中取出业务能力并分配到价值流中的价值流阶段；“实例化”业务能力时加入该能力产出成果所需的业务角色、应用组件、业务对象、业务流程与资源。 |
| 业务事件 | 业务相关状态变化；至少触发价值流，也可触发价值流阶段。 |
| 业务对象/数据对象 | 业务对象是特定业务域中使用的概念；数据对象是为自动化处理而结构化的数据。业务能力规划中的业务对象通常是可分配给一个或多个业务能力的概念对象，也可在应用组件中表示为数据对象。 |
| 业务流程 | 在业务能力实例语境中实现特定结果（如一组产品/业务服务）的业务行为序列。 |
| 业务角色 | 在业务能力实例的业务流程中执行特定行为的责任，或在整个价值阶段中参与所有业务能力的责任；可把参与者分配给该角色，也指参与者在特定行动或事件中所扮演的部分。 |
| 目标 | 组织及利益相关者关于意图、方向或期望终态的高层陈述；在能力规划中通常是特定价值流或阶段的高层意图。 |
| 成果 | 某种事态的最终结果、效果或后果；在能力规划中表示价值流/阶段的成果，以及判断其成功完成的方式。 |
| 资源 | 个人或组织拥有或控制的资产。 |
| 利益相关者 | 个人、团队或组织（或其类别）在架构影响方面利益的角色。 |
| 价值 | 概念的相对价值、效用或重要性；在能力规划中表示价值流（价值主张）或阶段（价值项）对一个或多个利益相关者的相对价值。 |
| 价值流/阶段 | 为客户、利益相关者或最终用户创造整体结果的活动序列；同一对象用于建模整体价值流与阶段。 |

### 3.2 ArchiMate 关系

在示例中，多数关系通过元素嵌套隐含表达——关系仍然存在，只是不显式。元素间关系的映射非常重要，这也是几乎必须使用建模工具的原因。模型目录对追溯相互依赖、执行业务能力规划分析至关重要。

### 3.3 架构建模工具

要正确执行业务能力规划，架构建模工具必不可少。业务目标与成果、能力实例以及成功交付客户价值所需组织资源之间的关系与依赖会迅速变得难以掌控，若无跟踪与维护方法将难以为继。

更大的收益在于整体元素目录与模型库：使用经过治理的元素目录、并查看这些互联模型在其他架构视图中的表达，可获得跨全部企业架构域的洞察。

> 示例中作者使用了开源 Archi 工具及 Co-Archi 扩展，模型存储库可从 The Open Group Library 获取。

---

## 4. 做好功课

任何业务能力规划活动都应从理解业务如何运作开始。对组织以下方面的良好理解有助于业务能力规划。许多组织中这些制品可能并不存在正式文档，需由从业者创建以完成分析。以下内容对整个组织（大型组织则对各业务领域分别）至关重要：

- 组织结构；
- 业务模型及相关业务对象；
- 当前战略、业务与财务计划；
- 应用与信息对象。

以下各节说明这些信息如何支撑业务能力规划的各个方面，并解释局限、给出示例（通过零售组织示例展开）。

### 4.1 组织结构

组织往往以与业务能力紧密对齐的方式构建：人员执行流程，并分配资金、IT 或其他公司资产等资源或工具。因此，企业的组织结构可用于启发能力目录。虽有对齐，但并不完全。

例如，多个业务单元通过业务能力实例参与创建或交付业务能力；有时组织单元按地域或客户细分对齐。组织结构自然也远比业务能力更易变。凡有可能，应避免使标示业务单元的功能名称与业务能力名称形成紧密对应。

示例零售组织有四个主要职能领域，每个领域下设更小的部门，向上级业务单元汇报，如图 4-1 所示。在模型中，每个职能领域以 ArchiMate 语言表示为利益相关者，并在建模工具中通过把每个利益相关者嵌套到其组织上隶属的领域来表示层级。

![图 4-1（英文原图）](figs/zh/g233e_fig4-1_zh.png)

> 图 4-1。图内文字已中文化；原图见英文原文 Figure 4-1。

**图内标签对照**

| 图内英文 | 中文 |
|---|---|
| Retail Organization | 零售组织 |
| Finance | 财务 |
| Accounts Payable | 应付账款 |
| Accounts Receivable | 应收账款 |
| Cash Management | 现金管理 |
| Payroll | 薪资 |
| Supply Chain Management | 供应链管理 |
| Purchasing | 采购 |
| Warehouse Management | 仓库管理 |
| Clothing Warehouses | 服装仓库 |
| Electronics Warehouses | 电子产品仓库 |
| Distribution | 分销 |
| Sales | 销售 |
| Retail Stores | 零售门店 |
| Region A | 区域 A |
| Region B | 区域 B |
| Region C | 区域 C |
| Region D | 区域 D |
| Internet Store | 网上商店 |
| Human Resources | 人力资源 |
| Talent Management | 人才管理 |
| Recruiting | 招聘 |

在这一层级，组织架构图尚未细到足以真正支撑整体能力目录，但更细层级可能可以。它确实指示了业务能力可能存在的位置。例如，财务之下有现金管理、应收账款与应付账款三项职能，对多数组织而言这些就是业务能力。在仓库管理与零售门店等领域，由于它们按地域划分、或在本例中按产品划分，组织层级并不能为业务能力目录提供启示。

### 4.2 业务模型

一种常见且简单的业务模型是商业模式画布（Business Model Canvas™）。把业务模型保持在抽象层级，可获得宏观视图，既易于沟通，又通常能提供在更细层级不易察觉的洞察。

Archi 中以画布形式提供商业模式画布。图 4-2 展示了虚构零售组织的版本。对于关键活动（Key Activities），请使用本文档后文所述的价值流。

![图 4-2（中文重绘）](figs/zh/g233e_fig4-2_zh.svg)

> 图 4-2：图内文字已中文化；结构据英文原图重绘。

**图内标签对照**

| 图内英文 | 中文 |
|---|---|
| Key Partnerships | 关键合作伙伴 |
| Product Vendors | 产品供应商 |
| Suppliers | 供应商 |
| Credit Card Processor | 信用卡处理商 |
| Shareholders | 股东 |
| Creditors | 债权人 |
| Key Activities | 关键活动 |
| Retail (Online) with Capability Instances | 零售（线上）及能力实例 |
| Retail (Physical) with Capability Instances | 零售（实体）及能力实例 |
| Recruit Employee Value Stream with Capability Instances | 招聘员工价值流及能力实例 |
| Key Resources | 关键资源 |
| Clothing Warehouse | 服装仓库 |
| Electronics Warehouse | 电子产品仓库 |
| Value Propositions | 价值主张 |
| Luxury feel at an affordable price | 以可负担的价格获得奢华感受 |
| Customer Relationships | 客户关系 |
| Expert advice | 专家建议 |
| Channels | 渠道 |
| Retail Store | 零售门店 |
| Website | 网站 |
| Mobile App | 移动应用 |
| Customer Segments | 客户细分 |
| Middle Class | 中产阶级 |
| Cost Structure | 成本结构 |
| Real Estate | 房地产 |
| Human Resources | 人力资源 |
| Inventory | 库存 |
| Revenue Streams | 收入来源 |
| Retail Sales | 零售销售 |
| Product Vendor Incentives | 产品供应商激励 |

通常会有许多有形的业务对象，它们是业务运作方式的核心。其中许多业务对象也会以一个或多个关键数据元素的形式体现在应用中。以下是一些零售导向的业务对象示例：

- **销售单据（Bill of sale）**：特定交易中所售商品的清单；
- **财务收据（Financial receipt）**：零售商与客户之间资金转移的记录；
- **目录（Catalog）**：零售组织可供销售商品的清单；
- **广告传单（Advertising flyer）**：目录的子集，用于突出特定商品，组织借此以优惠券提供激励，以提升产品销售。

对零售组织而言，适用以下度量：

- **网站转化率（Website conversion rate）**：访问网站并完成购买的访客百分比；
- **激励产品销量（Sales of incentivized products）**：使用优惠券完成购买的客户百分比；
- **订单到发货时间（Order to ship time）**：从下单到可被承运商取件所需的时长；
- **职位招聘时间（Recruit position time）**：从职位获批到雇用新员工所需的时长。

这些关键指标之所以重要，是因为它们通常决定了不同利益相关者或角色的动机，而这些动机可能并未在其他任何地方被清晰表达。就其自身而言，关键绩效指标（KPI）对业务能力规划并无用处，除非存在可与之关联、且同样可应用于价值流模型的可度量目标。

### 4.3 财务、业务与战略计划

以下三项通常可从财务计划中直接获得，但可能还需要更明确的业务计划与战略计划。

#### 4.3.1 财务报表（Financial Statement）

追踪资金在组织内的流动方式，可以洞察某一业务的哪些方面相对其他方面更重要或不那么重要。财务报表的编制结构也提供了对各种利益相关者所期望的动机与成果的洞察。最后，财务报表通常还能揭示某些价值流的运行效果可能未达到组织需要的领域。

section_title: 4.3.2 业务和/或战略计划（Business and/or Strategic Plans）
text:
#### 4.3.2 业务和/或战略计划（Business and/or Strategic Plans）

业务计划基于对业务所处市场的一定说明，叙述该业务打算做什么。它通常是财务报表的配套文件。战略计划通常针对某一内部或外部刺激而制定，代表为改变组织方向而进行的增量调整或资源转移。任何已陈述的目标或目的，既有助于确定重点领域，也会成为业务能力规划模型的一部分。

#### 4.3.3 平衡计分卡（Balanced Scorecard）

衡量业务绩效最具杠杆效应的工具是平衡计分卡。关于如何创建平衡计分卡，已有许多资源可供参考。就业务能力规划而言，它通常是目标与可度量目的的来源。

图 4-3 中，目标已与平衡计分卡的各个维度对齐；由某一特定目标实现的目的也已建立链接。

section_title: 4.4 应用目录、信息对象与交换
text:
### 4.4 应用目录、信息对象与交换

理解组织的应用目录，以及信息对象在应用之间是否交换、如何交换，是一项关键的“功课”，将在业务能力规划的分析阶段提供帮助。

section_title: 4.4.1 零售组织应用目录（Retail Organization Application Catalog）
text:
#### 4.4.1 零售组织应用目录（Retail Organization Application Catalog）

以下应用在该零售组织中用于实例化 Acquire Retail Product Online 价值流所需的业务能力：

- **客户关系管理（CRM）**：CRM 应用为零售商提供管理客户名单、客户身份、购买历史及其与组织其他交互的功能。
- **供应链管理（SCM）**：SCM 应用支持向实体门店分销产品以及履行在线订单的物流。
- **遗留仓库管理（Legacy Warehouse Management）**：该零售组织近期收购了一家电子产品分销商，其自有库存管理应用已使用近十年，集成功能有限。
- **现代仓库管理（Modern Warehouse Management）**：该应用目前仅管理服装库存；可扩展以处理电子产品，并已有一些尚未配置与其他应用集成的 API。
- **在线商店（Online Store）**：该应用提供浏览器与移动应用用户体验；它需要与其他应用建立接口，以维持良好的客户体验。
- **会计（Accounting）**：该应用管理组织的全部财务，包括应收账款与应付账款。
- **人力资源（HR）**：HR 应用管理员工招聘与管理的各个方面。
- **商业银行（Commercial Banking）**：该应用提供支持在线与店内支付的网关。
- **身份与访问管理（IAM）**：组织有一个企业 IAM 应用，目前支持员工身份，但不支持客户身份。

text:
#### 4.4.2 概念数据模型（Conceptual Data Model）

随着企业资源规划（ERP）与数据仓库的出现，已有许多行业标准的数据或信息模型，可在创建业务能力目录时使用。多数概念数据模型是业务对象及其相互关系的集合。以下业务对象视图（图 4-4）为简化的零售概念数据模型提供了基础。

section_title: 4.4.3 应用信息交换目录（Application Information Exchange Catalog）
text:
#### 4.4.3 应用信息交换目录（Application Information Exchange Catalog）

有了应用目录与概念数据模型，就可以完成对信息如何在事务层面与运营层面进行交换的评估。重要的是考察所有形式的信息交换。在这一分析层级，数据在应用之间移动的机制并不那么重要。

| （同上） | 客户（Customer） | — |

---

## 5. 价值流

“价值”（value）一词源自古法语 valoir，意为“值得”。它指某事物被认为应得的重视，即某事物的重要性、价值或有用性。在业务架构语境中，重要的是从有用性、优势、收益或合意性这一最一般意义上理解价值，而不是采用狭义的会计或财务视角——那种视角把价值定义为某事物的物质或货币价值。商业世界中非货币形式的价值包括：成功交付所要求的产品或服务、及时解决客户问题，或获得最新信息以做出更好的业务决策。

价值是组织一切活动的基础。组织存在的主要理由，就是向一个或多个利益相关者提供价值。价值是企业业务模型的基础，业务模型描述了企业如何创造、交付并获取价值的逻辑。业务架构师或企业架构师应能够对企业在特定利益相关者身上实现价值的多种方式进行建模、度量与分析，其中包括把价值的创造、获取与交付分解为若干离散的价值生产活动阶段的能力，每个阶段都依靠业务能力的有效应用来使能。

section_title: 5.1 业务能力规划中的价值流
text:
### 5.1 业务能力规划中的价值流

业务架构中所采用的价值分析方法源自 James Martin 的《大转型：运用企业工程七学科》[Martin, 1995]。价值流被描述为一组端到端的增值活动，为客户、利益相关者或最终用户创造整体结果。就建模而言，这些增值活动由价值流阶段表示，每个阶段都相对于前一阶段创造并增加增量式的利益相关者价值。

价值流可由外部触发，例如下文示例中零售客户购买商品；也可由内部触发，例如上文所示经理获得新雇员。价值流可在企业层面或业务单元层面定义；无论哪种情况，完整的价值流集合都标志着组织的主要业务活动集合，是企业为其各类利益相关者创造价值的多种方式的汇总。

价值流的一项关键原则是：价值始终从利益相关者的视角定义——即由工作所产出的产品、服务或交付物的客户、最终用户或接收者。所获得的价值取决于观察者眼中；它更多地取决于利益相关者对产品、服务、成果或交付物价值的感知，而非其内在价值（即生产成本）。

#### 5.1.1 描述价值流

价值流通常用包含以下五个要素的模型表示：

- **名称（Name）**：价值流名称必须从发起利益相关者的视角清晰可理解。与业务能力的命名方式不同，价值流使用主动语态而非被动语态，通常采用“动词—名词”结构。例如，本文档贯穿使用的两个价值流是“Acquire Retail Product Online”（在线获取零售产品）与“Recruit Employee”（招聘员工）。
- **描述（Description）**：名称应不言自明，简短、精确的描述可进一步说明价值流所处理活动的范围。
- **触发（Trigger）**：是什么业务事件导致该价值流启动？
- **利益相关者（Stakeholder）**：接收价值流所交付价值的人或角色。
- **价值项（Value Item）**：利益相关者期望在价值流成功完成后获得的价值（以利益相关者的语言表达）。

表 5-1 给出了由该示例展开的价值流要素：

**表 5-1：Acquire Retail Product Online 价值流旅程图**

| 要素 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 名称 | Acquire Retail Product Online（at Online Store） |
| 描述 | 寻找、选择、购买并获得所需零售产品所涉及的活动。 |
| 触发 | 客户访问网站。 |
| 利益相关者 | 希望购买产品的零售购物者（客户）。 |
| 价值项（Value Item / Value Generated） | 客户能够找到所需产品并及时获得。 |

#### 5.1.2 描述价值流阶段

利益相关者价值很少由单一步骤或活动产生。更常见的是，价值通过一系列顺序和/或并行的行动——即价值流阶段——来实现，每个阶段相对于前一阶段增量地创造并增加利益相关者价值；见图 5-1。

![图 5-1（英文原图）](figs/zh/g233e_fig5-1_zh.png)

> 图 5-1。图内文字已中文化；原图见英文原文 Figure 5-1。

**图内标签对照**

| 图内英文 | 中文 |
|---|---|
| Warehouse Order Fulfillment Value Stream | 仓库订单履约价值流 |
| Customer Order Placed | 客户下单 |
| Customer | 客户 |
| Customer Order Processing | 客户订单处理 |
| Pick Ordered Products | 拣选所订产品 |
| Pack Ordered Products | 包装所订产品 |
| Ship Ordered Products | 发运所订产品 |
| Order shipped within one business day | 订单在一个工作日内发运 |

每个价值流阶段包含以下要素：名称（2–3 个词，说明该阶段实现什么）、描述（几句话，说明阶段目的与执行的活动）、进入标准（触发该阶段或使其可启动的起始条件或状态变化；实践中通常是前一阶段的既有状态，对第一个阶段则是价值流启动的实际触发）、退出标准（表示阶段完成、所需价值已创建或交付给利益相关者的终态条件；许多情况下阶段名称与退出标准几乎相同）、价值项（该阶段创造或交付给参与利益相关者的增量价值）。

价值流并不一定从启动到结束连续不断地流动；如果所需价值尚未创建或交付，可在任一阶段停止，既可能是触发利益相关者要求停止，也可能是执行价值流的利益相关者决定停止。例如，客户在看到价格后决定不再购买，Acquire Retail Product Online 价值流即可停止。

---

## 6. 业务能力

在 The Open Group 中，能力（capability）被定义为“做某事的能力”。业务能力表示企业做某事的能力。更正式的定义如下：

组织所拥有的一种能力。能力通常以概括、高层次的术语表述，并需要人员、流程与工具的结合才能实现。

关键在于，业务能力界定企业“做什么”，而不试图解释企业如何、为何或在何处使用该能力。这些细节只有在该业务能力被映射到一个或多个价值流或价值流阶段、并对业务能力如何被实例化进行建模之后才会浮现。在评估一个或多个价值流相对于组织所定义的绩效指标的运行情况时，这一业务能力实例将十分关键。

业务能力可以是今天已经存在的能力，也可以是为使能新价值流或新战略而需要的能力；它还可能是组织随业务条件变化而决定消除的能力。汇编为目录后，业务能力代表企业为经营其业务可支配的全部能力。

### 6.1 定义业务能力

定义业务能力包括识别并描述企业为支持其整体使命需要做什么。业务能力的描述并不暗示某事应如何完成，只表明它需要存在。如何描述业务能力被实例化将在 6.4 节中演示。以下指南说明如何定义单个业务能力。

#### 6.1.1 命名约定

为业务能力命名是能力定义流程的第一步。它表明该业务能力有明确的存在必要，并有助于确保其与其他业务能力清晰区分。

命名约定要求以“名词—动词”格式表达业务能力：每个成果（输入、输出或交付物）用名词描述，而与产出、控制或监控该成果相关的每项活动用动词描述；例如“Catalog Products”（产品编目）或“Payment Processing”（支付处理）。业务能力的名词部分是一个唯一的业务对象——业务所关注的单一、持久的事物。以业务对象作为业务能力的焦点，其优势在于可简化识别与该业务对象绑定并被该业务能力使用的信息对象的过程。

业务对象通常是可触摸的——如“客户”或“贷款”——但也可能更概念化、更无形，如“研究”。最重要的考虑是使用能引起业务领导者与利益相关者共鸣的名称：普遍理解的名称能带来更好的理解，并改善不同利益相关者群体之间的沟通。然而，不建议简单照搬组织部门名称。与业务能力（本质上是稳定的）不同，组织结构并不持久，在多数组织中会频繁变化。

#### 6.1.2 描述

简短描述有助于阐明业务能力的范围与目的，并使其与其他业务能力区分。一种有用的句式是把每项业务能力的描述表述为“……的能力（或才能）”。例如，名为“Catalog Products”的业务能力可描述为：“维护一份经过整理、并与元数据交叉引用的产品或服务清单的能力”。

与业务能力名称一样，所有描述都应使用与业务利益相关者相关且适当的语言。有两项重要考虑：

- **简洁**：用一两句话提供刚好足够的细节，使人获得比仅凭业务能力名称更多的理解；
- **精确**：不要在描述中简单重复业务能力的名称。例如，描述“Program Management”时不要使用“管理项目群的能力”，而应表述为：“作为团队的一部分发起、计划、执行、控制并完成工作，以达成特定目标与成功标准的能力”。

### 6.2 业务能力目录

创建业务能力目录的目标，是捕获并记录使企业当前执行的价值流（无论执行得如何）或希望未来实施的价值流得以运行的那些业务能力。

第二步是以逻辑方式组织这些信息。识别初始业务能力集有三种方法：自上而下（top-down）、自下而上（bottom-up）与增量式（incremental）：

- **自上而下**：从企业层面识别 20 至 30 项最高层业务能力。高层业务领导者可在最初阶段帮助制定顶层业务能力。实践中，自上而下制定业务能力地图草稿更省时，但通常只有在组织高层领导者实质性参与时才会成功。并购或全面转型举措等影响整个组织的事件，是尚未开展业务能力规划时启动该项工作的合适时机。
- **自下而上**：时间较充裕时，可从业务各部门内部定义业务能力，自下而上构建。若没有强有力的治理与高层领导对构建企业级业务能力目录的支持，这种方法在整个企业范围内更难协调一致。
- **增量式**：当业务架构从业者真正开始应用业务能力目录中的内容时，目录必然会演进。把业务能力映射到价值流阶段，或细化到业务能力实例，会显示哪些业务能力可能缺失，以及目录中需要哪些冗余消除或新增。

业务能力目录代表覆盖相关业务、企业或组织单元的完整、稳定的业务能力集合。分析或咨询过程的最终产物通常是一份带定义的业务能力目录。业务能力目录视图有助于形成组织运行所需全部业务能力的可视描述。为便于导航，能力目录按类别或视角进行逻辑分组，以支持有效分析与规划。

能力目录需要足够大以具有包容性，又要足够小以便有效导航，并可用于映射到价值流与价值流阶段、以及描述为业务能力实例。一般而言，当能力目录超过 100 项时，很可能这些“业务能力”实际描述的是业务能力实例、能力实例的组件，或某些情况下的价值流阶段。

一旦定义完成，业务能力目录就提供了一个自包含的业务视图，独立于当前组织结构、业务流程、IT 系统与应用以及产品或服务组合。当价值流及相关业务能力如何实例化的具体细节尚不存在时，这种整体视图对规划很有用。

业务能力目录的策展需要相当多的工作，尤其在初期。通常由两到四人的小型团队起步较为有效，人数更多可能拖慢进程。从一开始就建立变更管理流程，用于评审拟新增、修订与删除的业务能力，并在进入运营后持续执行，会很有帮助。

#### 6.2.1 业务能力目录模型

以下业务能力目录模型（图 6-1）以可视化方式展示了基于本文档所述业务能力所形成的整体业务能力目录。

section_title: 6.3 把业务能力映射到价值流阶段
text:
### 6.3 把业务能力映射到价值流阶段

使用第 5 章定义的价值流，下一步是识别每个价值流阶段需要哪些业务能力来使能（图 6-2）：查阅业务能力地图，把相关业务能力链接（交叉映射）到每个价值流阶段。

该活动的目的是识别（在全部能力中）哪些业务能力对交付利益相关者价值至关重要，因而需要实例化到足够质量水平以满足利益相关者期望。

![图 6-2：把业务能力映射到价值流阶段](figs/g233_fig6-2.svg)

### 6.4 业务能力实例

价值流中捕获的业务能力被定义为**实例**。这样可正确捕获组织不同领域使用的能力，否则这些能力会在能力目录中冲突或重复。

对价值流的能力实例建模，可提供创建、增强或合并业务能力以改进价值流执行所需的洞察。记录参与者、利益相关者、资源、应用或流程的差距后，即可规划交付这些能力增量所需的投资计划。

对企业架构师而言，能力实例提供 TOGAF 各域之间的链接，价值流提供业务语境与需求；理解信息系统与技术如何使能这些能力实例，提供了连接后续 ADM 阶段的线索。

#### 6.4.1 能力实例指南

如今，组织已拥有以各类概念目录形式存在的组件清单，包括：

- 业务能力目录
- 应用目录
- 价值流目录
- 组织战略目标与成果

为完成分析，必须对受影响价值流的能力实例进行建模。能力实例是业务能力到该能力实例所需资源、应用和流程的映射。利用建模工具（如 Archi）中维护的各类目录，可使建模过程变得容易得多、快捷得多。

对业务能力实例建模，并非要对每个能力实例做穷尽式分解。组件选择应当讲述一个故事：至少需要什么，价值流才能从头到尾成功执行。同时可以预期，企业架构存储库中还会有其他模型可供分析，包括专门针对应用、技术环境和详细技术节点的视图；这些视图会更详细地说明应用被设计用于执行、并被分布部署以执行的功能。

借助上文确定的业务能力目录，可以在业务能力内部添加人员、流程和资源组件。使用嵌套而非箭头，可提升模型的可读性与清晰度。随着组件不断添加，更多业务能力实例会随之自然显现——或表现为同一业务能力的多个实例，或表现为在进入下一层细节之前未曾发现的能力缺口。

用能力实例为价值流建模，可避免业务能力目录膨胀。许多组织会在目录中创建业务能力的“特化”，而这些特化实际上反映的是某些业务能力被实例化的方式。有时，随着业务能力目录的元素增多，这一点显而易见；但目录膨胀通常发生在层级中把一项业务能力分解为更多业务能力之处。

最后是业务能力交互这一概念。该组件的使用应限于 ArchiMate 信息流关系。能够包含在单个应用之内、且跨越多个业务能力实例的信息流，无需单独标识。信息流可以是两个应用之间的程序化数据交换，也可以是“转椅式”接口——由某人把数据从一个应用转录到另一个应用（在 ArchiMate 语言中表示为数据对象），或者是人与人之间通过口头、或通过交换纸质/类纸制品进行的交互（表示为业务对象）。

section_title: 6.4.2 Acquire Retail Product Online 价值流
text:
#### 6.4.2 Acquire Retail Product Online 价值流

现在用一个示例说明以上内容。该示例展示通过在线商店进行零售购买的处理过程。为快速完成分析，许多目录必不可少，包括业务能力目录、应用目录与企业数据模型（用于表示业务对象和数据对象）。最后，组织战略及相关目标与目的将指导所选价值流应如何改变，以实现预期业务结果。

在查看模型本身之前，以下叙述更详细地描述各价值流阶段。

section_title: 6.4.2.1 浏览在线商店（Browse Online Store）
text:
##### 6.4.2.1 浏览在线商店（Browse Online Store）

浏览任何零售商店时，布局都是整个购买体验的一部分。商店入口与布局经过规划，与布局关联的产品也经过规划。如果客户身份已知，布局可根据其偏好调整。此阶段通常还会展示可用的激励。该阶段的成功标准是客户能够找到其正在寻找的产品。

section_title: 6.4.2.2 选择要购买的产品（Select Product(s) for Purchase）
text:
##### 6.4.2.2 选择要购买的产品（Select Product(s) for Purchase）

客户找到所需产品后，可根据所选产品的属性（如尺寸、颜色或其他属性）进入更细的层级。此时他们可能还关心产品是否在仓库中有货。完成产品配置后，客户可将其加入购物篮，这标志着该价值流阶段的完成。

值得注意的是，价值流不必按顺序执行。客户可以选择回到价值流起点并循环多次。同样，客户也可以跳过某一步，例如不查看购物篮而直接结账。

##### 6.4.2.3 查看购物篮（Review Basket）

在此阶段，客户可以查看已放入购物篮的商品，决定更改数量，并查看基于购物篮内容可应用的激励。该阶段以客户选择继续支付产品费用而结束。

##### 6.4.2.4 购买产品（Purchase Products）

所需产品选定后，接下来确认交付选项与支付详情。此时客户必须提供身份信息，可以一次性提供，也可以注册以便未来复用，包括加入零售商忠诚度计划等功能。配送选择通常会影响购买总成本，因此先于最终输入支付信息以处理交易。该阶段结束时，客户会收到所购产品的发票以及付款收据。

##### 6.4.2.5 交付产品（Deliver Products）

购买完成后，可执行最后一个价值流阶段。在此阶段，产品从仓库拣选并包装待运。包裹被配送组织取件后，生成运输跟踪号。当承运商确认包裹已交付给客户时，该价值流阶段及整个价值流结束。

图 6-3 展示了把上述叙述建模为价值流中的业务能力实例后的样子。

## 7. 业务能力规划

本文档写于新冠疫情期间。疫情引发并持续引发的创新是多年来世界最大的阶跃变化之一，零售业也不例外：没有在线履约机制的组织要么创建该新价值流，要么消亡；实体零售店增加了客户自提等机制以减少物理接触。

组织中的企业架构师可用本文档技术，构想利用现有能力实例的新价值流，并在需要时促进新能力实例或改进能力实例的开发，使新价值流成功执行。

疫情期间这些新价值流被快速建立，通常使用成熟度较低的能力实例、并以大量人工干预执行。通过本文档的技术与模型，组织可迭代改进能力实例成熟度以优化新价值流，或在业务条件不再需要时退役该价值流及相关能力实例。

### 7.1 能力实例分析方法

改进能力实例本身不是目的。在以下任何规划情景中评估能力实例，都必须以改进能力所实例化的价值流为依归；应优先增强能带来价值流改进、达成组织既定目标的能力实例。

以组织平衡计分卡为例，与“在线获取零售产品”价值流直接对齐的成果是“使用优惠券的人数增加 1%”；而更多回头客的成果将依赖另一个营销价值流来驱动流量，从而触发本价值流。

四种规划情景：

- **优化（Optimize）**：最常见，改变能力实例的一个或多个组件；
- **整合（Consolidate）**：次常见，通常通过应用合理化与/或重组实现；常用于并购后或重组场景；
- **新建（Create）**：业务格局变化可催生全新价值流和/或新能力与能力实例，扩展价值流的触达或速度；需防止重复建设，或至少有意图地建设；
- **退役（Retire）**：所有能力实例退役的情况较少见；此时整体业务能力从组织能力目录中移除——需谨慎确认利用该能力实例的未识别价值流不受影响。

#### 7.1.1 优化能力实例

识别每项业务能力中需增强或废弃的具体部分，并在模型中标记为“缺口”以便进一步分析。基于受影响能力组件的一套一致缺口类型可使规划更容易。示例缺口类型：

- **应用增强**：全新应用，或现有应用增加/废弃功能；
- **业务流程变更**：修改现有流程或创建新流程；
- **资源变更**：增加或移除能力实例所需的“有形”资源；
- **角色/利益相关者变更**：有时重组谁支持各能力实例是合理的——可增加某部分组织内的职责，或把能力实例职责重新分配给更专业的组织领域；
- **信息/数据对象**：信息时代信息为王；价值流执行的根本往往在于能力实例之间数据传递很少甚至没有，或数据不完整、不正确。

零售组织示例：决定优化“配送管理”能力实例，让配送司机使用签名板确认订单。

#### 7.1.2 整合能力实例

整合能力实例很常见，尤其在并购之后。从 IT 视角看，这表现为应用和/或技术合理化过程，且往往缺少价值流视角。许多情况下整合能力实例确实有助于组织目标；退役其中一个实例以实现节约是合理化的一大驱动。

通过包含价值流分析的业务能力规划，可识别整合能力实例的潜在风险：可能影响利用该能力实例的其他价值流——可能发生在两个价值流交织的价值流层，也可能仅在能力实例层。

在零售组织中存在两个库存管理应用。这是并购造成的结果：两个不同的仓库使用两套不同的库存管理应用。为简化订购流程，公司决定整合现代仓库管理应用而非遗留仓库管理应用，因为遗留仓库管理应用更难以集成到 CRM 应用。

#### 7.1.3 新建能力实例

组织通过复用已有业务能力来增强或创建新价值流的能力，是整体成功的关键。所有组织都不可避免地会因各种原因而演进。业务能力规划确保只有在价值流语境中确有需要时才创建业务能力实例。

复用业务能力实例通常是最佳实践，但有时创建新的业务能力实例也是有益的。许多成熟的业务能力实例对一个或多个价值流至关重要，或者其实例化方式使该实例难以快速增强。最后，也可能存在某个特定价值流和/或业务能力实例仅在短期内需要的情况。

在零售组织中，他们希望为网站增加激励，以尝试带动更多购买。这需要一个新的业务能力实例，因为该组织已经实施了激励管理。当前的激励是面向实体门店的优惠券，通过 CRM 应用以电子邮件发送给已登记加入组织邮件列表的客户。这个新实例需要一个与在线商店应用的接口，以向任何网站访客展示通用激励，并向通过身份验证的访客展示个性化激励。

#### 7.1.4 退役能力实例

业务能力的最后一种选择是退役，既可作为优化价值流的一部分，也可在组织决定停止执行某特定价值流时进行。在这种情景下，理解使用某一特定能力的全部价值流，对风险缓解很重要。

section_title: 7.2 规划业务能力实例增量
text:
### 7.2 规划业务能力实例增量

业务能力往往无法一步达到最终期望状态。还可能存在依赖关系，意味着能力增量的顺序需要协调。根据需要解决的差距，可能存在这样的顺序：业务流程变更需要先于应用增强发生。无论这些依赖关系带来何种逐步变化，一起解决的一个或多个差距将被识别为一个 **plateau（平台期）**；也就是说，为解决这些差距而进行的一组增强，能够保持价值流的功能完整。

架构模型能够识别存在差距的业务能力，以及这些差距可能存在的依赖关系。资源管理以及由谁通过工作包交付业务能力增强的时间安排，留给项目或项目群负责。差距使用 ArchiMate 的 **gap 元素**表示；把同一个 gap 分配给多个业务能力，表示它们可能属于同一分组。

回顾上一节的业务能力改进，可建模如下：

- **优化（Optimize）**：通过为配送司机提供签名板（Signature Pad）并把签名回传至运输应用，增强 Delivery Management 业务能力实例；该差距在业务能力层面看似很小，但设计与实施需要一些时间。
- **整合（Consolidate）**：升级 Modern Warehouse Management 实例，使其包含 Electronics Warehouse 的产品。这些已在应用层建模为差距。Modern Warehouse Management 应用增强后，使用 Legacy Inventory Management 应用的 Inventory Management 实例即可退役。
- **新建（Create）**：向第一个价值流新增一个 Incentive Management 能力实例，如图 7-2 所示。
- **退役（Retire）**：同样在图 7-2 中于应用层展示。许多业务能力及相关价值流依赖 Legacy Warehouse Management 应用。由于 Legacy Warehouse Management 应用并不存在真正的“差距”，用事件“Retire Application”标记该应用。

借助已识别的差距，项目经理或运营团队可利用模型，根据团队容量确认时间安排，并在必要时突出会影响这些差距处理顺序的依赖关系。

示例中的差距彼此独立，唯一例外是退役那个由 Legacy Warehouse Management 应用实例化的 Warehouse Management 业务能力。也会出现这样的情况：识别出一系列差距，它们都是价值流有效执行所必需的。这意味着许多团队必须使用标准项目管理实践或更协调的运营发布管理来协同工作。

section_title: 7.3 数字转型与业务能力规划
text:
### 7.3 数字转型与业务能力规划

数字转型有时被视为一种与其他创新形式不相称的特殊创新形式。这种看法由多种因素造成，包括技术变革的速度、组织无法以同样的速度适应，以及对变革的恐惧——这种恐惧阻碍了大多数创新的采用。业务能力规划有可能使数字转型不那么令人生畏、更可实现：全新的价值流虽可能出现，但通常是增强或创建新的能力实例，并与可更快实施的现有能力实例组合。以价值流与业务能力为视角，新技术可被置于“利益相关者如何使用组织价值流”的语境中，而不是让技术本身成为缺乏语境的焦点。

技术——如同用于创建或增强能力实例的其他资源——实际上是现有能力实例的一个组件。借助业务能力规划模型与技术，企业架构师与业务架构师可以更有效地展示如何最佳利用这些新技术。

## 8. 结论

业务能力规划可以成为业务架构师与企业架构师的有力工具。理解价值流是能够开展业务能力规划的关键第一步。创建并策划业务能力目录，可提供一套术语词典，以支持不同利益相关者之间的对话。

把业务能力关联到价值流，再对这些业务能力如何被实例化进行建模，可为进一步分析提供基础。通过改变业务能力实例，可以优化价值流。

---

section_title: 附录 A：业务能力目录
text:
## 附录 A：业务能力目录

以下定义为本文档示例中所用业务能力提供了定义。

| 业务能力 | 定义 |
|---|---|
| Accounts Payable（应付账款） | 管理为收到货物或服务而付款的能力。 |
| Basket Management（购物篮管理） | 选择待结账与支付的产品或服务的能力。 |
| Benefits Management（福利管理） | 为员工提供非工资性福利的能力。 |
| Business Planning（业务规划） | 确定方向以聚焦资源，并评估达成既定目标与目的之进展的能力。 |
| Catalog Products（产品编目） | 维护分类的产品或服务清单的能力。 |
| Compensation Management（薪酬管理） | 以金钱或其他经济价值交换货物或劳动而给予个人的能力。 |
| Contract Management（合同管理） | 与供应商及供货方谈判、监控、续签并终止合同的能力。 |
| Customer Relationship Management（客户关系管理） | 跨多个接触渠道与方法监控并发起客户互动的能力。 |
| Delivery Management（交付管理） | 追踪货物和/或人员从起点到最终目的地的地理位置的能力。 |
| Finance Management（财务管理） | 以符合法律法规要求的方式管理资金、投资、资产与负债的能力。 |
| Human Resources Management（人力资源管理） | 为组织招聘、雇用、培养、付酬并分配人员执行活动的能力。 |
| Identity Management（身份管理） | 解析个人或事物身份的能力。 |
| Incentive Management（激励管理） | 管理财务或其他奖励以影响员工、供应商或客户行为的能力。 |
| Inventory Management（库存管理） | 规划并管理货物从供应商到存储地点、再从这些地点到使用或处置点的流动的能力。 |
| Job Posting（职位发布） | 在组织内发布空缺职位的能力。 |
| Market Research（市场研究） | 评估可能影响组织业务计划的组织、产品与服务供给的竞争格局的能力。 |
| Payment Processing（支付处理） | 管理向收款方转移资金的能力。 |
| Payroll Management（薪资管理） | 定期向员工付酬，并遵守该员工所在司法辖区的法律与法规的能力。 |
| Position Management（职位管理） | 维护职位目录的能力，目录包含成为特定职位合适候选人所需的技能、经验与认证。 |
| Product Development（产品开发） | 研究、设计并寻源可销售给其他组织或人员的产品或服务的能力。 |
| Program Management（项目群管理） | 作为团队的一部分发起、计划、执行、控制并完成工作，以达成特定目标与成功标准的能力。 |
| Risk Management（风险管理） | 识别、评估并排序不确定性，进而配置资源以最小化、监控并控制不幸事件发生概率和/或影响的能力。 |
| Schedule Management（日程管理） | 协调人员与资源的时间安排，使其在特定时间与地点可用的能力。 |
| Skills Assessment（技能评估） | 判断个人技能与能力成熟度的能力。 |
| Store Layout Management（门店布局管理） | 设计客户在门店中的行进方式，以便发现、选择并购买产品的能力。 |

## 附录 B：其他框架

业务能力规划可作为派生其他模型、并与其他框架衔接的基础。本附录说明使用价值流的业务能力规划如何为这些框架提供输入，其中部分章节会指出相似术语的使用之处，并说明其差异。

### B.1 业务流程建模

业务流程模型比价值流与业务能力具有更少的正式边界或条件。业务流程模型可与价值流或底层业务能力紧密对齐，也可松散对齐。使用业务能力实例可以提供参与者与许多粗粒度步骤，随后可下钻到更深层级，以获得更详细的依赖与规格。

业务过程或应用过程是业务能力实例的组件之一。系统分析师可能在此层级建模，以构建应用中所需的特定业务逻辑；但业务分析师很少在业务能力实例层级建模流程。

更常见的做法是在价值流阶段层级创建业务流程。使用 BPMN™（Business Process Model and Notation™）或所选业务流程建模语言，可以在顺序图与泳道图中详述参与者与应用交互。更详细的业务流程建模正是在此既受价值流启发，也为价值流提供输入。

有些业务流程会跨越价值流阶段。许多业务流程仅从人类参与者视角编写；有些则为每个参与者单独编写以支持培训。把业务能力实例中描述的流程加以统一并不值得投入；但让分析师与架构师共同评审其模型，则确实值得投入。

section_title: B.2 Scaled Agile Framework 企业价值流
text:
### B.2 Scaled Agile Framework 企业价值流

Scaled Agile Framework® 企业版（SAFe®）旨在帮助那些希望“……使用精益、敏捷与 DevOps 实现业务敏捷”的组织。[1] 若您的组织属于此类，业务能力规划可作为有价值的补充，用于创建运营价值流（见下文）以及定义敏捷发布列车（Agile Release Train）。

**SAFe 运营价值流**[2]

在 SAFe 中，价值流概念与本文档所述有许多相同方面。SAFe 描述两类价值流：运营价值流与开发价值流。运营价值流本质上就是本文档所描述的内容。开发价值流则描述使能开发增强或新 IT 资产的价值流及支撑性业务能力实例，这些资产旨在改进各项业务能力实例，从而简化并优化运营价值流。

正如 SAFe 网站所述：“……多数 SAFe 指南聚焦于帮助系统与软件开发人员、产品经理、工程师、科学家、IT 从业者以及其他在开发价值流中工作的人员……然而，他们所服务的客户要么位于公司内部，要么处在运营价值流的末端。”

采用敏捷或 SAFe 实践的组织，可以在业务能力实例层面运用业务能力规划，把运营价值流与开发价值流连接起来。

**敏捷发布列车**[3]与运营价值流

敏捷发布列车旨在按敏捷产品管理团队所共享或支持的运营价值流或开发价值流，对其待办列表与增强进行对齐。对于业务能力规划中的运营价值流，Acquire Retail Product Online 价值流所提出的全部增强都将加入各受影响产品团队的待办列表。

在零售组织中，CRM、在线商店、现代仓库管理与遗留仓库管理应用团队都是不同的敏捷团队。所提出的增强将形成两列发布列车，每列都需要两个团队之间的协调。

第一列发布列车是打通“在线商店激励管理集成”与 CRM 之间差距的增强。敏捷团队可将所建议的高层业务能力实例改进进一步分解为适当的产品增强并纳入产品待办列表。由此可确定拟议的产品发布计划，并传达给相应利益相关者。敏捷发布列车将迭代推进，直至支撑该价值流各业务能力实例所需的增强全部完成，并且这些增强所实现的价值可被度量。

第二列发布列车出现在电子产品仓库能够迁移使用现代仓库管理应用、遗留仓库管理应用团队可以退役该应用之时。这列发布列车会更复杂，因为这两个应用所支撑的运营价值流远多于 Acquire Retail Product Online 一个价值流。这同样是业务能力规划能够帮助采用 SAFe 的组织，基于各组合建立相互依赖路线图之处。

### B.3 旅程地图

价值流通常由从中获得价值的利益相关者触发。旅程地图是对某一利益相关者在一系列接触点上体验的分析，以理解该体验如何改进。旅程地图可与价值流阶段及底层业务能力实例对齐，用于分析与改进价值流。

表 B-1 展示了基于 Acquire Retail Product Online 价值流的旅程地图。旅程地图通过考察正在研究阶段中的客户体验来扩展价值流；此处仅针对在线购买，不含最后一个价值流阶段。相关接触点被加入并评估，随后可按照业务能力规划框架，把改进领域映射回需要修改的能力实例。

**表 B-1：旅程地图——Acquire Retail Product Online 价值流**

| 客户画像：新客户 | 场景：搜索广告产品以获取折扣，并首次建立账户 |
|---|---|

| 接触点 | 到达网站 | 浏览产品 | 选择产品 | 查看购物篮 | 支付购买 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 用户想法或感受 | | | | | |
| 改进机会 | | | | | |
| 受影响的业务能力实例组件 | | | | | |

### B.4 精益价值流

精益价值流源自精益思维运动，该运动发端于日本汽车业（在丰田，该过程被称为“物料与信息流图”）。精益思维的核心前提是识别并消除企业流程中的浪费，目标只保留能为最终用户创造或增加价值的活动。精益价值流是以图解方式表示设计、生产并向客户交付商品或服务所需的活动序列（见图 B-1）。通过为每个流程添加绩效指标（如处理时间、响应时间与完成准确率），便可用精益价值流识别减少浪费的机会。

精益价值流的主要目的是记录、分析并改进为客户生产产品或服务所需的信息或物料流动。这似乎也与业务能力规划的理由相一致。于是不可避免地产生一个问题：如果目的相一致，技术手段是否也能一致？

精益六西格玛[4]领域有一个关键缩写 SIPOC（Suppliers、Inputs、Processes、Outputs、Customers，即供应商、输入、流程、输出、客户）。考察业务能力规划的价值流，它会覆盖利益相关者、目标与成果。再看上述模型，流程与职能被组合起来以支持某种形式的分析。

运用业务能力规划技术，可借助围绕前置时间与处理时间的精益浪费概念，考察每项业务能力实例在支撑特定价值流阶段或整个价值流时的运行效率。

### B.5 Porter 价值链

价值链由 Michael Porter 在其《竞争优势：创造并维持卓越绩效》一书中提出 [Porter, 2004]；见图 B-1。

“价值链把企业分解为若干战略相关活动，以理解成本行为及现有的（竞争）差异化潜在来源。”

![图 B-1（中文图）](figs/zh/g233e_figB-1_zh.png)

> 图 B-1。图内文字已中文化；原图见英文原文 Figure B-1。

**图内标签对照**

| 图内英文 | 中文 |
|---|---|
| Support Activities | 支持活动 |
| Firm Infrastructure | 企业基础设施 |
| Human Resource Management | 人力资源管理 |
| Technology Development | 技术开发 |
| Procurement | 采购 |
| Primary Activities | 主要活动 |
| Inbound Logistics | 入站物流 |
| Operations | 运营 |
| Outbound Logistics | 出站物流 |
| Marketing And Sales | 市场营销与销售 |
| Service | 服务 |
| Margin | 利润 |

价值链视角主要关注活动成本与利润，致力于理解经济价值如何被创造。价值链提供企业如何生产经济价值（即金钱）的宏观视图。与商业模式画布一样，价值链通常对整个组织或业务单元建模。从该视角看，价值链可作为决策依据，用以确定需要建模哪些价值流以确保价值链运行。

### B.6 风险与安全视角

风险与安全视角贯穿整个组织。可能存在某些专属于安全的业务能力，如身份管理；也可能表现为使某项业务能力实例得以运行的流程，或价值流执行的目标与成果；它还可能是价值流本身，例如零售组织内发生盗窃调查之时。

《TOGAF® 系列指南：在 TOGAF 企业架构中集成风险与安全》[G152] 提供了安全控制指南及其与其他标准的关联。

section_title: 附录 C：Recruit Employee 价值流
text:
## 附录 C：Recruit Employee 价值流

Recruit Employee 价值流在本文档编写过程的早期即已开发。作者后来决定示例聚焦于更以客户为中心的价值流。尽管如此，既然工作已经完成，纳入这个更偏后台的示例仍有价值。

从组织战略可见，他们追求收入增长。这意味着吸引并雇用新员工的能力对组织整体成功至关重要。目前，该价值流的执行时间是组织要求的两倍多。此外，当最终候选人入职后，还出现了一些技能差距。该价值流需要缩短当前执行时间，并改善所发布职位与最终成功候选人之间在技能与经验上的匹配。

该价值流被分解为以下五个价值流阶段（亦见图 C-1）。价值流在出现空缺职位时启动——无论是新设职位，还是员工离职：

- **定义职位（Define Position）**：招聘经理在其负责的项目群内，审视团队所需的角色。

  HR 顾问查阅现有角色目录与职位描述，利用其中一项或多项调整出职位描述。最后，财务分析师确认该职位有足够的薪酬预算。

- **发布空缺职位（Communicate Open Position）**：招聘人员依据职位描述在招聘应用中创建职位，随后发布到公司网站及一家签约职位发布网站。

  候选人通过任一渠道提交简历与求职信，随后被迁移至文档库。HR 顾问人工审阅每份简历，剔除不合格候选人，以得到一份“可管理”的候选人名单。

- **筛选最终候选人（Select Final Candidates）**：由招聘经理与 HR 顾问组成的团队审阅候选人短名单并打分，以选出进入面试的短名单。

  入围候选人被安排并接受面试。随后调整评分，形成一份将发出录用通知的候选人排名名单。

- **发出职位录用（Offer Position）**：查阅现有薪资带宽，为创建雇佣合同提供必要输入；合同连同入职前信息文件一并发送给候选人。

  完成该价值流阶段还需要最终的警方背景核查以及已签署的合同。

- **候选人入职（Onboard Candidates）**：候选人到岗工作时，为其提供办公空间、凭据，并完成薪资与福利信息的最终确认。

  此时，该员工尚未准备好履行其受雇承担的职责。

对该价值流阶段的初步分析表明，每个阶段需要以下业务能力；同时补充了阶段终点、关键利益相关者、价值流触发条件，以及改进该价值流的目标。

图 C-1 对该价值流及业务能力实例进行了建模。

section_title: The TOGAF® Standard, a Standard of The Open Group
text:
The TOGAF® Standard, a Standard of The Open Group

The TOGAF Standard is a proven enterprise methodology and framework used by the world’s leading organizations to improve business efficiency.

This Document

This document is the TOGAF® Series Guide to Information Architecture: Metadata Management. It has been developed and approved by The Open Group.

The information shared in this document has been gathered from the lessons learnt on the ground (best practices and pitfalls) from several projects.

More information is available, along with a number of tools, guides, and other resources, at www.opengroup.org/architecture.

About the TOGAF® Series Guides

The TOGAF® Series Guides contain guidance on how to use the TOGAF Standard and how to adapt it to fulfill specific needs.

The TOGAF® Series Guides are expected to be the most rapidly developing part of the TOGAF Standard and are positioned as the guidance part of the standard. While the TOGAF Fundamental Content is expected to be long-lived and stable, guidance on the use of the TOGAF Standard can be industry, architectural style, purpose, and problem-specific. For example, the stakeholders, concerns, views, and supporting models required to support the transformation of an extended enterprise may be significantly different than those used to support the transition of an in-house IT environment to the cloud; both will use the Architecture Development Method (ADM), start with an Architecture Vision, and develop a Target Architecture on the way to an Implementation and Migration Plan. The TOGAF Fundamental Content remains the essential scaffolding across industry, domain, and style.

1. Introduction

In this document, information architecture best practices are shared to support architecture work on the specific topic of Metadata Management. It aims to provide a framework to:

• Accelerate the delivery of architecture study

• Inform Data Architects and other data professionals about good practices

• Provide a common language to describe the Metadata Management capability to data professionals: Chief Data Officers, Data Managers, Architects, Data Engineers, and Data Scientists

Metadata Management is instrumental in delivering value from data. This document intends also to emphasize the benefits of data documentation, and the necessary efforts required to set up an effective Metadata Management capability within an organization.

2.1. The ArchiMate® Specification

This document uses the formal notation from the ArchiMate Specification [C226] to describe the Metadata Management architecture reference models.

The ArchiMate elements used in this document are shown in Figure 2-1.

Figure 2-1: The ArchiMate Modeling Notation Elements Used in This Document

The ArchiMate definitions of each concept used in this document are as follows:

Motivation Aspect

• Goal: represents a high-level statement of intent, direction, or desired end state for an organization and its stakeholders

• Requirement: represents a statement of need defining a property that applies to a specific system as described by the architecture

Business Layer

• Business role: represents the responsibility for performing specific behavior, to which an actor can be assigned, or the part an actor plays in a particular action or event

• Business function: represents a collection of business behavior based on a chosen set of criteria (typically required business resources and/or competencies), closely aligned to an organization, but not necessarily explicitly governed by the organization

• Business Collaboration: represents an aggregate of two or more business internal active structure elements that work together to perform collective behavior

section_title: 2.2. The TOGAF® Standard and Data Architecture
text:
2.2. The TOGAF® Standard and Data Architecture

This document proposes:

• A focus on Metadata Management to guide the design of the capability including reference models with business function and application function descriptions (see Chapter 5 and Section 5.2)

• An adaptation of the TOGAF ADM phases [C220] to support the execution of a Metadata Management transformation program (see Chapter 4)

3. Metadata Management Capability

Simplistically, metadata can be called “data about data”. For example, metadata indicates who is the author/creator of the data, when it was created, its security classification, its data quality attributes, and so on. According to the Data Management Body of Knowledge (DMBOK2), pp.417 [DMBOK2]:

“Metadata helps an organization understand its data, its systems, and its workflows. It enables quality assessment and is integral to the management of databases and other applications. It contributes to the ability to process, maintain, integrate, secure, audit, and govern other data.”

The concept of metadata is not new and is widely used in the IT industry to define data about data. In ancient times long before the digital age, metadata such as author, title, number of tablets, etc. was already used to catalog collections of clay tablets. As such, metadata provides additional information to better know and use the data.

Metadata Management is the planning, implementation, and control activity that enables access to high-quality, integrated metadata [DMBOK2]. It enhances the data with additional information so that it can be used to:

• Know your data:

◦Reduce uncertainty and possible misinterpretation of the data

◦Know the quality of the data available and associated business rules (data quality business

rules, transformation business rules, etc.)

◦Data origin and usage of the data

◦Improve auditing of Business Intelligence (BI) reports

◦Monitor data volume across the information system to reduce environmental impact

• Manage the data risk and compliance with regulatory requirements:

◦Leverage data classification (confidentiality, privacy) to support data risk management (e.g., to

support data protection impact assessment), base data access model on defined metadata (e.g., roles, responsibility of the user, purpose of data processing, etc.)

◦Leverage security and privacy metadata for the enterprise’s most valuable asset; for example:

▪Security metadata enables the transition from network-centric to attribute-centric security

embodied in new standards such as zero trust that treat data as a corporate asset

▪Enterprise identity management relies on a federated identity (common attributes) to

control human or machine access to data

▪Privacy legislation in many countries and/or groups of countries (e.g., the European Union)

makes the dissemination of personally attributable data illegal

◦Improve auditing of data lineage and usage to meet regulatory requirements

• Manage data lifecycle:

◦Need metadata to indicate what is required to adhere to enterprise policies and directives

◦Need to know what must be archived and retained as a record (often a function of national

legislation)

◦Need to identify retention lifecycle to trigger disposition (deletion)

• Improve time-to-market:

◦For any new business initiative, reduce data scoping effort with the support of good data

documentation (glossary, dictionary, classification)

◦Identify relevant data elements for use cases

• Manage data quality and sharing :

◦Enable information interoperability/sharing to facilitate enterprise and extraprise

collaboration, shared (situational awareness), and decision support

◦Identify redundant and obsolete data

◦Support the business to leverage external data

Metadata is all too often delegated to IT, whereas it is essentially a business concern. Subsequent to numerous investigations in the mid-2000s and new government legislation, metadata is a key corporate asset that has to be maintained to ensure shareholder transparency, corporate security, and client privacy.

The rise of NoSQL databases (relaxed data schemas) and the recent big data trends with the associated promise to unlock value from any kind of data, have led to focus solely on building the capabilities to collect, store, and analyze the data. Very little effort was put on metadata which is often depicted as irrelevant or available automatically using machine learning tools. Beyond market trends, Metadata Management is still a challenge in many organizations for multiple reasons:

• IT complexity:

◦Legacy applications are poorly documented: reference data is lacking, and data changes its

meaning during the lifecycle of the application

◦Mergers and acquisitions are increasing the IT landscape and therefore the scope of metadata

to be documented is changing

◦The replication factor: this concept defines how many times a data element (e.g., customer first

name) is replicated in the information system; the higher the replication factor, the more challenging the metadata documentation effort

• Data complexity:

◦Variety and velocity of data collected (e.g., social media feeds or logs collected near real-time,

text and image collected for machine learning purpose, etc.) require new techniques to collect the relevant metadata

◦Dynamic schemas make it challenging to maintain up-to-date metadata documentation

• IT marketing trends:

◦Microservices/micro applications often challenge data lineage and increase the replication

factor

◦“Agile” delivery is incorrectly interpreted as no requirement for documentation

• Manual work:

◦How to capture the information with business and IT Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs)?

◦What is the right granularity and priority criteria?

◦Metadata validation is not automatic and needs a human review

• Lack of data standards:

◦Naming conventions

◦Data types and unit conventions

However, metadata is key from a business perspective to having good knowledge and understanding of the data already available within the organization. Therefore, metadata is an important foundational data management capacity for any organization looking to efficiently leverage its data.

In the effort to design this capability, we have focused on the minimum set of functions required to effectively deliver Metadata Management. As an organization becomes more mature in the practice, it is possible to go beyond the baseline defined in this framework. We also believe that ethical use of data is becoming more and more important for every organization. It is reflected in the regulations taken in several parts of the world following the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR),[1] which came into force in the EU on May 25, 2018. Even more than compliance to regulatory requirements, it can be a competitive advantage for the organizations that document data usage by design to enable data governance over ethical use of data. Therefore, we have included in this baseline framework “data usage documentation” in the Metadata Management business functions, with an emphasize on personal data.

This section covers the high-level reference model functions and their definitions. More detailed functions are available in the dedicated reference model part of this document in Chapter 5 and Section 5.2.

3.1. Metadata Management High-Level Reference Model

Figure 3-1: Metadata Management Capability – High-Level Functions

the organization or the distribution of the metadata to other applications. | Endnotes [1] Refer to: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Data_Protection_Regulation.
4. Process and Methodology

section_title: 4.1. TOGAF Adaptation for a Metadata Management Capability
text:
4.1. TOGAF Adaptation for a Metadata Management Capability This chapter describes a synthesis of key actions related to the TOGAF ADM phases (Preliminary, A, B, C, D, E, F) that should be performed in the context of a Metadata Management capability delivery. | TOGAF ADM Phase | Metadata Management Recommendation | | --- | --- | | Preliminary Phase | Make sure that the data owners or any business stakeholders with clear metadata business
requirements are identified to support the architecture work.
Make sure that there is an architecture governance board well integrated with other data
governance and operational data boards. This is to ensure that the architecture decisions are
consistent with the organization data strategy and data management activities.
Ensure that the outputs of the architecture work can be operationalized during the
implementation phase via a design authority. | | Phase A:
Architecture Vision | Clarify the business drivers to document metadata and the business goals that will be
achieved.
Capture the business use cases that will be supported by the Metadata Management capability,
the priorities, and the business actor requirements.
Assess the maturity of the organization in relation to Metadata Management practice, existing
pain points if any, and expected improvements.
Develop an overview of:
• The metadata sources available within the organization
• The existing communities (business and technical actors) around each metadata source
• The metadata lifecycle (create, modify, delete) within each source and related Metadata
Management processes of each community
Define the scope of metadata required to deliver the business requirements and to support
data governance in accordance with the organization’s data strategy. Clarify the level of
metadata, community, and metadata process integration required.
Create an enterprise metadata policy including a conceptual metadata model.
Develop the value proposition of the target Metadata Management capability taking into
consideration the business use cases, organization maturity, existing pain points, metadata
sources available, and the level of integration required. |

section_title: 4.1. TOGAF Adaptation for a Metadata Management Capability
text:
| TOGAF ADM Phase | Metadata Management Recommendation | | --- | --- | | Phase B:
Business Architecture | Leverage known regulatory requirements, other internal and external compliance
requirements, business use case requirements, business data issues, and available data sets to
formalize metadata requirements.
Define key metadata assets to be documented to support the business requirements.
Capture the level of metadata quality required per scope of metadata.
Identify the as-is (baseline) and to-be (target) business users of the Metadata Management
capability, the related roles, and access requirements.
Formalize the organization and detailed Metadata Management processes that should be
implemented in the target with the support of the Data Management Office.
Clarify the set of business functions that are required to deliver the business requirements and
perform the baseline versus target gap analysis. The business reference model provided in
Chapter 5 can be used as a guide for this step.
Refer to Section 4.2 for further details about the metadata requirements, the metadata model,
and Metadata Management processes. |

section_title: 4.1. TOGAF Adaptation for a Metadata Management Capability
text:
| TOGAF ADM Phase | Metadata Management Recommendation | | --- | --- | | Phase C:
Information Systems
Architectures | Extend the conceptual metadata model into the logical level (attributes and domains specified)
and then map the conceptual metadata entities or attributes to the logical data model entities,
records (tuples/instances), or attributes.
Define the metadata integration model, clarifying:
• The scope of metadata that is managed within the target metadata repository that will
support data governance
• Primary/secondary roles between the target metadata repository and the existing
metadata sources within the organization
• The collaboration contract for metadata exchange between the target repository and other
sources of metadata
Define the metadata collection approach that is relevant in the target: manual ingestion,
pushing metadata from sources, pulling metadata from sources.
Clarify the metadata inference requirements (if any) and the level of complexity pertaining to
this inference. Data variety (structured, semi-structured, unstructured) and IT landscape are
two important factors of metadata inference complexity.
One of the key challenges about data documentation is to document the data lifecycle from its
origin as well as the movements and transformations it has been through in the information
systems. This is done through metadata associations and typically requires manual effort.
Therefore, clarify metadata association requirements based on business requirements to
concentrate the effort on the relevant scope.
Clarify the set of application functions that are required to deliver the business requirements
and perform the baseline versus target gap analysis. The application reference model provided
in Section 5.2 can be used as a guide for this step.
Refer to Section 4.3 for more details about this step. | | Phase D:
Technology
Architecture | Full coverage of the metadata IT capability may require multiple technologies to be combined.
Data integration vendors in general provide optimized connectors to extract the technical and
operational metadata from data integration repositories, database dictionaries, and data
patterns inside semi-structured and unstructured data. Data governance solutions are less

section_title: 4.1. TOGAF Adaptation for a Metadata Management Capability
text:
| TOGAF ADM Phase | Metadata Management Recommendation | | --- | --- | | Phase F:
Migration Planning | First, start documenting the metadata assets in a spreadsheet focusing on a small scope to
become familiar with the concepts and foster a documentation culture within the team.
Metadata documentation requires manual effort: business metadata is managed by people,
technical metadata exists in the data structures of the IT systems, operational metadata is
generated at a specific point in time. This first step should also aim to prove the value of
documenting metadata.
Next, move to a centralized repository to enforce metadata governance (stewardship,
ownership, validation workflow, etc.), scale metadata documentation, and ease metadata
access and administration management. A centralized repository has several benefits, such as
the ease of knowledge sharing and re-use by bringing the different stakeholders (business data
owner, data steward, internal controllers, data protection officer, data manager, etc.) into the
same repository, the ease of metadata association as all the assets are already collected into a
single repository, and the centralized metadata stewardship to support metadata governance.
However, a strong governance model enforced by the Data Management Office and the
onboarding of the different stakeholders (business data owner, data steward, internal
controllers, data protection officer, data manager, etc.) can be challenging as the repository
may not be dedicated to their role and specific needs.
The more mature the different stakeholders become, the more advanced requirements might
emerge such as automated data discovery (e.g., record linkage) and catalog, data flow
visualization, automated reverse engineering of data schemas, etc. At this stage, it can make
sense to consider dedicated repositories for different families of contributors to support their
specific requirements. This means that a dedicated system can be defined per logical group of
assets. For example, a repository for a business glossary, a repository for data dictionaries, a
repository for data quality rules documentation and implementation, etc. It is therefore
possible to provide advanced features dedicated to each metadata documentation function and
to support specific user interfaces customized for each role or family of users. However, a
dedicated effort should be put into metadata integration to link the metadata assets together,
ensure consistency between the repositories, and avoid silos. Also, collaboration between the
different stakeholders can be limited. | | Phase G:
Implementation
Governance | Organize a compliance review with Metadata Management projects (metadata repository
implementation, metadata integration) to check that they respect the principles and target
architecture. |

section_title: 4.2. Metadata Management Guidelines for a Business Architecture (ADM Phase B)
text:
4.2. Metadata Management Guidelines for a Business

Architecture (ADM Phase B)

Metadata is available in multiple sources within an organization; see Figure 4-1. The main challenge is to bring together different kinds of metadata, from different communities, with different processes and lifecycles, in order to achieve specific business goals such as data compliance, data quality monitoring, and data accessibility.

section_title: 4.2. Metadata Management Guidelines for a Business Architecture (ADM Phase B)
text:
Figure 4-1: Metadata Sources Illustration

(Metadata domains have been harvested from use cases and applied to the context of this document.)

Our recommendation is to engage in a step-by-step progressive approach to build the metadata documentation rather than attempt to document all the assets identified in the existing metadata sources at the same time.

4.2.1. Collect Metadata Requirements

There are different approaches to define metadata requirements (see Figure 4-2):

• A top-down approach starting with compliance or other business use cases to formalize metadata requirements; for example:

◦Compliance: Regulation (GDPR, Solvency II,[1] IFRS 17[2]), internal (digital sustainability, security

rules)

◦Business use cases: get customer interactions data to improve up-sell

• A bottom-up approach based on business data issues or data set requirements; for example:

◦Data set: document existing Customer Information File (CIF) to support BI & Analytics use cases

◦Business data issue: customers are invoiced at the wrong frequency generating frustrations and

complaints; investigate root causes to tackle the issue

Figure 4-2: Metadata Requirements Collection Illustration

The top-down approach (compliance, business use cases) often has strong business support; metadata consistency is required and guaranteed by validation processes and workflows. The bottom-up approach is more opportunistic and does not always have strong business support. For this approach it is important to show the value with concrete examples before further automation and governance. In both cases, it is important to clarify the metadata requirements including the expected level of metadata quality required.

4.2.2. Formalize Metadata Management Processes

Metadata quality is enforced by processes and validation workflows that can vary per metadata scope. There are mainly two approaches (see Figure 4-3):

• The normative approach, which aims to guarantee precision, accuracy, integrity, and consistency of the metadata

In this approach the metadata is created by a few, published as read-only, static (few changes overtime), and its lifecycle is managed via validation workflows. It fits well with metadata subject to regulatory constraints and central organization.

• The collaborative approach is more appropriate in the data democratization approach where there is a need to have multiple contributors maintaining the technical metadata and, when required, to associate the technical metadata with business metadata to provide a business context: created by many, edited by many, dynamic, eventual consistency
Figure 4-3: Metadata Quality Enforcement Approaches

section_title: 4.3. Metadata Management Guidelines for Information Systems Architectures (ADM Phase C)
text:
4.3. Metadata Management Guidelines for Information

Systems Architectures (ADM Phase C)

The metadata repository is supported by a Metadata Management IT solution, which is a combination of technologies (set of functions), a data model, and processes (metadata update and validation workflows) in order to support Metadata Management activities.

Figure 4-4: Metadata Management IT Solution

section_title: 4.3. Metadata Management Guidelines for Information Systems Architectures (ADM Phase C)
text:
The metadata data model formalizes the metadata requirements by clarifying the set of metadata assets that will be documented in the metadata repository and their relationships. As described in Section 4.2, the metadata validation workflows are designed to support metadata quality requirements.

Metadata is often divided into three categories that can be summarized as follows, based on the DMBOK2:

• Business metadata focuses largely on the content and condition of the data and includes details related to data governance

• Technical metadata provides information about the technical details of data, the systems that store data, and the processes that move it within and between systems

• Operational metadata describes details of the processing and accessing of data

Business metadata is managed by people, technical metadata exists in the data structures of the IT systems, and operational metadata is generated at a specific point in time. Figure 4-5 shows a baseline proposal of key metadata assets (see the definitions in Appendix A) to be captured to support data governance.

Figure 4-5: Key Metadata Assets

After identifying the metadata data assets to be documented, it is important to leverage the Dublin Core™ Metadata Element Set (DCMES) [DCMES] at the attribute level to effectively describe each asset. For instance, the subject field is key to making sure that metadata is universally discoverable throughout the enterprise. It is useful to have the tags correspond (map) to the logical data model elements, especially the generalization-specialization constructs (e.g., Sedan is a type of Car that is a type of vehicle) so that searches (and business rules) can find all of the requisite data for whatever purpose.

section_title: 4.3. Metadata Management Guidelines for Information Systems Architectures (ADM Phase C)
text:
Once the scope of metadata assets to be collected is defined, the metadata integration model needs to be clarified taking into consideration the broader scope of existing metadata sources and the business architecture outputs (business actors to be onboarded, metadata validation processes, data governance operating model). As stated in ISO/IEC 19773, “… it is a general description framework for data of any kind, in any organization, and for any purpose. ISO/IEC 19773 does not address other data management needs, such as data models, application specifications, programming code, program plans, business plans, and business policies.” [ISO/IEC 19773] The proposed framework here is to go beyond the ISO/IEC 19773 model by making explicit the key assets that are relevant to support data semantics documentation but also data management needs. section_title: 4.3. Metadata Management Guidelines for Information Systems Architectures (ADM Phase C)
text:
• Pushing metadata:

◦Initial effort to set up the extractors for each metadata source

◦Possible additional tool(s) required to support metadata integration

• Pulling metadata:

◦The metadata solution may have access to all the data; indeed, sometimes the tool will have

access to the data files to be able to infer the technical metadata

◦The metadata agent can be an intrusive component for critical applications

◦Security audit is required to ensure compliance with security policies as the metadata solution

will have read access to multiple applications in the information system landscape

The complexity to collect technical and operational metadata depends on the data variety and IT landscape, with a main difference when the data schema and operational metadata are defined by- design versus when the metadata is extracted a posteriori by leveraging analytical techniques (metadata inference, machine learning, etc.).

Figure 4-10: Technical Metadata Inference

• Structured data can be easily collected from database dictionaries, technical metadata stores, data integration repositories, etc.

Note that data schema collection does not require access to data.

• Semi-structured files come with a structure but do not guarantee schema stability over time as each file may have its own structure

• Unstructured data: we cannot manage what we do not know

A minimum structure (shapes in an image; email address from a document, etc.) must be extracted from the unstructured data before analysis and governance. Such an exercise requires scanning the data content which may involve intensive data processing if there are millions of files to scan.

section_title: 4.3. Metadata Management Guidelines for Information Systems Architectures (ADM Phase C)
text:
Multiple techniques/libraries/tools exist to extract technical and operational metadata from data; the tool selection depends on the kind of metadata that is needed, the complexity to extract the information, and the performance/volume of data to scan.

To a certain extent, managing metadata for unstructured data means first capturing the technical metadata; multiple structures can be extracted over time from the same unstructured data set. The main challenge is to maintain the associations with other metadata to put this unstructured data in context:

• Business meaning: association with the business terms, business data objects, business data elements

• Context of use: association with data processing activities

• Data quality requirement: association with business data quality rule, technical data quality rule, data quality anomaly

• Privacy requirement: association with data deletion rule, etc.

Endnotes

[1] Refer to: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solvency_II. [2] Refer to: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFRS_17.

### 2.1 ArchiMate® 规范

本文档使用 ArchiMate 规范 [C226] 的正式记法描述元数据管理架构参考模型。所用元素见图 2-1，定义如下：

**动机方面**

- **目标**（Goal）：对组织及其利益相关者而言，关于意图、方向或期望终态的高层陈述。
- **需求**（Requirement）：定义适用于架构所描述特定系统之属性的需求陈述。

**业务层**

- **业务角色**（Business Role）：代表执行特定行为的责任，可把参与者分配给该角色，或代表参与者在特定行动/事件中所扮演的部分。
- **业务功能**（Business Function）：基于一组选定标准（通常是所需业务资源和/或胜任力）的业务行为集合，与组织紧密对齐，但不一定由组织显式治理。
- **业务协作**（Business Collaboration）：两个或以上业务内部主动结构要素的聚合，共同执行集体行为。

**应用层**

- **应用功能**（Application Function）：可由应用组件执行的自动化行为。

## 3. 元数据管理能力

简单地说，元数据可以称为“关于数据的数据”。例如，元数据表明数据的作者/创建者、创建时间、安全分级、数据质量属性等。根据《数据管理知识体系》（DMBOK2）第 417 页：

> “元数据帮助组织理解其数据、系统与工作流。它使质量评估成为可能，是数据库及其他应用管理不可或缺的部分；它有助于处理、维护、集成、保护、审计与治理其他数据的能力。”

元数据概念并不新鲜，IT 业界广泛用它定义“关于数据的数据”。早在数字时代之前的古代，作者、标题、泥板数量等元数据就已用于编目泥板藏品。因此，元数据提供额外信息，以便更好地了解和使用数据。

**元数据管理**是使高质量、集成元数据可被访问的规划、实施与控制活动 [DMBOK2]。它用额外信息增强数据，使其可用于：

- **了解你的数据**：
  - 减少数据的不确定性与可能的误解；
  - 了解可用数据的质量及相关业务规则（数据质量业务规则、转换业务规则等）；
  - 了解数据来源与使用情况；
  - 改进 BI 报表审计；
  - 监控整个信息系统的数据量，以降低环境影响。
- **管理数据风险并符合监管要求**：
  - 利用数据分级（保密性、隐私）支持数据风险管理（如支持数据保护影响评估），基于已定义元数据建立数据访问模型（角色、用户责任、处理目的等）；
  - 为企业最有价值的资产利用安全与隐私元数据，例如：安全元数据支持从以网络为中心转向以属性为中心的安全（如零信任等新标准把数据视为企业资产）；企业身份管理依赖联邦身份（共同属性）控制人或机器对数据的访问；许多国家/地区的隐私立法（如欧盟）使可识别个人数据的传播成为非法；
  - 改进数据血缘与使用审计，以满足监管要求。
- **管理数据生命周期**：
  - 需要元数据表明遵循企业政策与指令所需的内容；
  - 需要知道哪些必须归档并作为记录保留（往往是国家立法的要求）；
  - 需要识别保留生命周期以触发处置（删除）。
- **缩短上市时间**：
  - 对任何新业务举措，借助良好的数据文档（术语表、字典、分级）减少数据范围界定工作；
  - 识别用例所需的相关数据元素。
- **管理数据质量与共享**：
  - 实现信息互操作/共享，促进企业及扩展企业的协作、共享（态势感知）与决策支持；
  - 识别冗余与过时数据；
  - 支持业务利用外部数据。

元数据常被推给 IT，但它本质上是业务关注点。2000 年代中期大量调查及新的政府立法之后，元数据已成为必须维护的关键企业资产，以确保股东透明度、企业安全与客户隐私。

NoSQL 数据库（宽松数据模式）的兴起与近期大数据趋势承诺从任何数据中释放价值，导致人们只关注建设采集、存储与分析数据的能力，很少投入元数据——常被视为无关紧要，或认为机器学习工具可自动获得。除市场趋势外，元数据管理在许多组织中仍是挑战，原因包括：

- **IT 复杂性**：遗留应用文档匮乏（参考数据缺失，数据在应用生命周期内含义变化）；并购扩大 IT 架构，需文档化的元数据范围随之变化；复制因子（某数据元素在信息系统中被复制的次数）越高，元数据文档化越难。
- **数据复杂性**：采集数据的多样性与速度（近实时社交媒体或日志、用于机器学习的文本与图像等）需要新技术采集相关元数据；动态模式使保持元数据文档最新变得困难。
- **IT 营销趋势**：微服务/微应用常挑战数据血缘并提高复制因子；“敏捷”交付被错误理解为不需要文档。
- **人工工作**：如何与业务和 IT 主题专家（SME）一起采集信息？正确的粒度与优先级标准是什么？元数据校验不自动，需要人工复核。
- **缺乏数据标准**：命名约定；数据类型与单位约定。

然而从业务视角看，元数据是良好了解和理解组织已有数据的关键。因此，对任何希望高效利用数据的组织而言，元数据是重要的基础数据管理能力。

在设计该能力时，我们聚焦有效交付元数据管理所需的最小功能集。随着组织实践成熟，可超越本框架定义的基线。我们还认为，数据的伦理使用对每个组织都越来越重要——这体现在 GDPR（《通用数据保护条例》，2018 年 5 月 25 日在欧盟生效）之后世界多地出台的法规中。比合规更重要的是，按设计记录数据使用、以实现对数据伦理使用的治理，可成为组织的竞争优势。因此，本基线框架在元数据管理业务功能中纳入了“数据使用文档”，并强调个人数据。

本节介绍高层参考模型功能及其定义。更详细的功能见本文档第 5 章与 5.2 节的参考模型部分。
